pageCache.text:
Engage, Enrich, Excel
Welcome to Beech Grove Primary School
It is a privilege to welcome you to our website and to our school.
We are incredibly proud of the inclusive, family feel we have fostered at Beech Grove and the strong links we have with our local community. We believe that every child deserves an outstanding education and we recognise our responsibility to deliver this. Whilst our goal of creating very literate and numerate children is central to our work, our aim is much bolder: to help develop socially confident, morally responsible individuals who are equipped to make a positive contribution to society and to live a fulfilled life.
Our Values
Parent and PupilTestimonials
This is a truly wonderful school where every child is valued, encouraged, and supported to be the very best they can be. The caring and dedicated staff create a warm, welcoming environment where children feel happy, confident, and inspired to learn. It is a place that genuinely nurtures both academic achievement and personal growth, making it a school that families can be proud to be part of. Vicki (parent)
The teachers are helpful, kind and caring. I have made some amazing friends, enjoyed exciting trips and learnt lots of new skills. I have learnt that working hard and never giving up helps you achieve your goals. Gwen (pupil)
Beech Grove Primary welcomed our son with open arms from his very first day. Rather than expecting him to fit a mould, they celebrated his differences, helping him grow in confidence and believe in himself. The staff genuinely care about every child, creating a warm, nurturing environment where childhood is cherished and children feel like they belong. It truly is a one-of-a-kind school. Rae & Chloe (parents)
One of my favourite parts of this school is the lessons are always practical and positive. I have very much enjoyed taking part in lessons and sports and I will always remember memories with teachers and the school in general and I think every teacher should be proud of themselves for how well they’ve taught us. Edward (pupil)

pageCache.pageTitle: Beech Grove Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
VISION AND VALUES
OUR SCHOOL VISION
Engage, Enrich, Excel
At Beech Grove, we are committed to working in partnership with parents to provide an engaging and enriching educational experience for all our pupils so that they excel academically and acquire the knowledge, skills and character they need to lead happy, fulfilled and successful lives. .
We ENGAGE our pupils in the joy of learning through a broad, balanced and inspiring curriculum that is driven by pupil needs and interests. We seek to develop our pupils as creative thinkers, problem solvers and collaborators who have the motivation, resilience and self-belief to shape their own futures and make a positive contribution to society.
We ENRICH our pupils' learning by connecting them to their local, national and global world and by opening doors to new experiences and opportunities. We recognise and nurture talent through specialist teaching in art, music and sport, while ensuring that all pupils have access to the experiences, relationships and opportunities that broaden horizons, build confidence and inspire ambition.
We support every pupil to EXCEL, regardless of their starting point, circumstances or the barriers they may face. We are committed to building an inclusive school where every child feels safe, valued, known and able to belong. Through high expectations, strong relationships and effective support, we seek to ensure that every pupil achieves ambitious outcomes and develops the independence and self-belief needed for future success.
Inclusion and Vulnerable Learners
Inclusion is not an additional aspect of our work; it is central to achieving our vision for every pupil.
At Beech Grove, we define a vulnerable learner as a child whose circumstances, experiences or needs create barriers to engaging in learning, benefiting from enrichment opportunities or achieving their full potential academically, socially, emotionally or personally.
We recognise that vulnerability may be temporary or long term, visible or hidden, and can change over time. A child may experience vulnerability because of factors relating to learning, health, emotional wellbeing, family circumstances, relationships, attendance or significant life events. We recognise that vulnerability cannot always be identified through labels, diagnoses or categories. Instead, we seek to understand how a child's circumstances, experiences and needs may affect their ability to access, participate in and benefit from school life.
To ensure that every child can engage, enrich and excel, we are committed to:
Developing a deep understanding of every pupil's strengths, interests, needs, experiences and goals.
Recognising barriers to participation, changes in presentation and emerging needs, and responding early and effectively when concerns arise.
Providing the relationships, support, adaptations and opportunities that enable every child to thrive and experience success.
Through knowing, noticing and nurturing every child, we work to remove barriers to learning and participation, strengthen inclusion and ensure that all pupils can access the full curriculum and wider opportunities available to them. We place pupil and staff wellbeing at the centre of our work, ensuring our vision and values are brought to life in everything we do.
Every child has strengths, talents and potential.
Inclusion is everyone's responsibility.
Strong relationships are fundamental to successful inclusion.
OUR CORE VALUES
Our six values sit at the heart of our thinking and decision making and guide us towards achieving our vision. They were chosen by our school community and the definitions were written by our Year 6 pupils. Our values are a weekly focus in our assemblies, curriculum teaching and in our day to day discussions with pupils.
Respect: Showing you care about the feelings, wishes and the rights of others. It can also be about admiring someone for their skills or qualities.
Responsibility: Being accountable for something. It is about accepting that you are in charge of your own behaviour and actions.
Resilience: The ability to recover quickly from things if they do not go as you planned. You have to believe in yourself, persevere and not be afraid to make mistakes.
Aspiration: The desire to turn hopes or dreams into reality. It is when you want to get better at something and do all you can in order to achieve this. If you have aspiration you have hope.
Courage: The ability to do something that frightens you. It is when you try something even though you know you might not be able to succeed. It is what helps you to overcome your fears.
Kindness: The quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate. Kindness is a gift. It is free, can come from anyone and brightens your day.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beech Grove Primary School - Wrap around childcare
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club (before school)
We are delighted to offer a Breakfast Club provision for all pupils.
Breakfast Club operates in two sessions, Monday to Friday:
A healthy breakfast is available during both sessions, providing children with a positive and settled start to the school day.
Places must be booked in advance to support staffing and catering arrangements.
If you wish to apply for a place at Breakfast club, please book via ParentPay: https://www.parentpay.com/
Squirrels (after school)
Squirrels is a carefully planned provision in which children have access to exciting and engaging activities such as: cooking, sewing, stories, outdoor games, crafts and music. Squirrels provides a 'homely' space, where children are given the freedom to choose which activities they would like to access. After a long day at school, some children like to be active outside whilst others prefer to relax and engage in something quieter. It is clear that the children love attending the club and it is something they look forward to each day.
Places are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

Governors
The Governing Board of Beech Grove Primary School has the following core, strategic functions:
1). Establishing the strategic direction, by:
2). Ensuring accountability, by:
3). Overseeing financial performance, by:
Governors usually serve a four-year term on the Governing Board. The role of Governors is now far reaching with wide-ranging responsibilities. In 2021, the Full Governing Board (FGB) decided to form a Finance Committee to further strengthen its commitment to financial oversight as shown in 3). above.
The school employs a Clerk to the Governors to keep accurate minutes of all discussions and to advise the Board of their statutory responsibilities.
A copy of all FGB meeting minutes are available from the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beech Grove Primary School - English Curriculum
pageCache.text:
English Curriculum
We follow a two year rolling programme in English based on the whole school approaches 'Talk for Writing' and 'Talk for Reading'.
Please follow the links below to see an overview of our English curriculum and progression in this subject:
Writing Overview Writing Progression Spelling Map Y2-6
Foundational knowledgeSentence Writing Progression
Phonics Progression Reading ProgressionGrammar Progression
Our Approach to Literacy
At Beech Grove Primary School, we believe that literacy has the power to transform lives. Through high-quality texts, rich vocabulary, purposeful discussion and meaningful writing experiences, we strive to develop confident readers, enthusiastic writers and effective communicators. We want every child to develop a lifelong love of literature, a strong command of language and the confidence to share their ideas with the world.
We place carefully chosen, high-quality literature at the heart of our English curriculum. Through stories, novels, poetry and non-fiction, children develop a love of reading, deepen their understanding of the world and learn how authors use language to inform, entertain and inspire. These same texts provide the foundation for our writing curriculum, enabling children to write with increasing confidence, accuracy and creativity.
Our approach is underpinned by Re-think Reading and BookWrites programmes, both of which place authentic, high-quality texts at the centre of learning. Through carefully sequenced teaching, children build strong mental models that enable them to make connections, apply learning confidently and become increasingly independent in their literacy journey. We ensure that all children develop secure transcription skills, including handwriting, spelling and sentence construction, through high-quality first teaching and carefully targeted interventions that build from each child’s individual starting point.
Reading
"Once you learn to read, you will be forever free." Frederick Douglass
Reading is at the very heart of our curriculum. We believe that reading enables children to access the wider curriculum, develop their understanding of the world and build the vocabulary they need to communicate effectively.
Early Reading and Phonics
In Reception and Key Stage 1, children are taught through the Read Write Inc. phonics programme. Daily phonics lessons provide children with the knowledge and skills needed to become accurate and fluent readers.
We are committed to ensuring that every child becomes a successful reader. Where additional support is needed, carefully targeted interventions enable children to build on their starting points and secure the essential knowledge and skills required for future success.
From Key Stage 1 and throughout Key Stage 2, reading is taught through Re-think Reading approach. Using high-quality whole texts, including novels, picture books, poetry and non-fiction, children develop comprehension, vocabulary and a deep understanding of literature. Children discuss, question, infer, explain and respond thoughtfully to what they read, helping them become reflective and enthusiastic readers.
Children are encouraged to discuss and explain their ideas, ask and answer thoughtful questions, develop vocabulary through rich texts, justify opinions using evidence and read increasingly complex literature.
Writing
️ "Writing is the painting of the voice." Voltaire
In Reception, children begin their journey as writers through Drawing Club in Reception class. Using high-quality stories and engaging experiences, Drawing Club encourages children to listen, talk, imagine, draw and create. Rich vocabulary, storytelling and discussion sit at the heart of every session, helping children develop confidence as communicators and fostering a love of writing from the very beginning.
We believe that enthusiasm, creativity and a positive attitude towards writing are essential foundations for future success. The excitement and engagement developed through Drawing Club provide the building blocks for children's continued development as writers throughout Key Stage 1 and beyond.
At Beech Grove Primary School, writing is taught through the BookWrites approach. BookWrites uses carefully selected, high-quality children's literature as the stimulus for learning and provides a structured sequence that enables children to develop both the craft of writing and a love of language. Children learn to write by studying the choices made by skilled authors before applying these techniques in their own writing.
At the beginning of each writing sequence, children complete an independent writing task. This enables teachers to identify existing knowledge and tailor learning to meet the needs of the class.
Children become immersed in the model text through reading, discussion, vocabulary exploration and close analysis. They learn to understand how authors achieve particular effects and begin to identify the techniques that make writing successful.
Teachers explicitly model the writing process, demonstrating how authors make choices and craft their work. Children apply their learning through shared and guided writing activities before moving towards greater independence.
Children use their knowledge of the model text to create their own pieces of writing. They plan, draft, revise and edit their work, making thoughtful authorial choices and developing increasing independence as writers.
Handwriting, Spelling and Transcription
We recognise that strong transcription skills are essential for children to write fluently and effectively.
Handwriting is taught through the Read Write Inc. Handwriting programme, which provides a clear progression from the mark-making and letter formation skills developed in Reception through to fluent, legible handwriting across Key Stages 1 and 2. We carefully monitor progress and provide a range of targeted and individualised interventions to ensure that every child develops secure transcription skills from their own starting point.
Children also receive explicit teaching in spelling, grammar and sentence construction. By securing these foundational skills, children are better able to focus on composition, creativity and authorial intent.
Speaking and Listening
"If you can tell a story, ask a question and share an idea, you have the tools to change the world."
At Beech Grove Primary School, we recognise that spoken language is fundamental to learning. Through purposeful discussion, children develop the vocabulary, confidence and communication skills needed to become successful readers, writers and learners.
Children are provided with regular opportunities to discuss texts and share ideas, explain and justify their thinking, ask and answer thoughtful questions, build on the contributions of others, present their learning, apply ambitious vocabulary and participate confidently in collaborative learning.
High-quality classroom discussion is woven throughout the curriculum. Through book talk, partner talk, collaborative tasks and curriculum-based discussions, children learn to listen carefully, communicate clearly and express themselves with increasing confidence and precision.
Reading for Pleasure and Enrichment
Developing a lifelong love of reading and writing is one of our key priorities. Throughout the year, children enjoy a wide range of enrichment opportunities designed to celebrate literacy and inspire a passion for books and storytelling.
These include author and illustrator visits, visits from the local library, World Book Day celebrations, daily opportunities to enjoy high-quality class texts and whole-school writing days every half term.
These experiences help children see themselves as readers and writers, broaden their horizons and create lasting memories linked to literacy.

History
Year A OverviewYear B Overview History Progression History SequencingKey Concepts Key Concept Progression History Curriculum Timeline
History helps us understand yesterday so that we can shape tomorrow.
At Beech Grove, we believe that history helps children make sense of the world they live in. As the driver subject for our autumn term theme, 'Discover', history inspires pupils to ask questions, investigate evidence and uncover the fascinating stories and events that have shaped our local community, our country and the wider world. We equip children with the knowledge, understanding and curiosity to recognise that history is far more than learning about dates and famous people; it is about discovering how the choices, achievements and experiences of the past continue to influence our lives today.
Through rich enquiries, high-quality historical sources and memorable learning experiences, we develop children's understanding of chronology, cause and consequence, change and continuity, similarity and difference, significance and interpretation. We teach pupils to think like historians by analysing evidence, questioning interpretations, considering different viewpoints and making informed judgements based on the evidence they encounter. In doing so, children learn that history is not simply about remembering the past, but about understanding how we know what we know.
Learning is enriched through meaningful local history, educational visits and opportunities to investigate artefacts, photographs, maps and original historical sources. We foster a strong sense of identity and belonging by enabling children to discover the story of their own community while recognising how Britain's past connects with the wider world. Through these experiences, pupils develop empathy, appreciate the diversity of human experience and understand that history continues to shape the society in which we live.
Through engaging opportunities to discover the past, pupils are enriched by stories that inspire curiosity, deepen understanding and encourage critical thinking, developing the confidence to excel as thoughtful, reflective and informed historians.

Modern Foreign Languages
Year A & B OverviewsFrench ProgressionKnowledge Organisers
At its heart, learning a language is about communicating with others, discovering different cultures and seeing the world from new perspectives.
At Beech Grove, we believe that learning another language opens children’s minds to a wider world and gives them the confidence to communicate beyond their own language and culture. Our curriculum, supported by the Primary Languages Network, progressively develops children’s vocabulary, pronunciation and understanding so that they become increasingly confident in listening, speaking, reading and writing in French. Through their learning, children also develop curiosity about France, French-speaking communities and different ways of life, recognising that language and culture are closely connected.
Through an ambitious and carefully sequenced curriculum, we teach children to think and communicate like language learners. They listen carefully for meaning, recognise patterns and sounds, develop accurate pronunciation and intonation, ask and answer questions and gradually learn to express their own ideas, preferences and opinions. As their confidence grows, children read and understand increasingly complex language, write phrases and sentences from memory and manipulate familiar vocabulary and grammatical structures to communicate with greater independence. They explore how French works by noticing connections and differences between French and English, developing their understanding of grammar, gender, word order and verb forms alongside strategies for working out unfamiliar language.
Learning is enriched through stories, songs, rhymes, games and meaningful contexts that allow children to experience French as a living language rather than simply a collection of words to remember. Children encounter aspects of French life and culture through celebrations, food, places, everyday routines and leisure, while using language for practical purposes such as describing themselves, expressing opinions, shopping, ordering food and sharing information. The children enjoy opportunities to encounter and sing in other European languages and celebrate the richness and diversity of languages beyond French during European Day of Languages. Through these experiences, children develop confidence in taking risks with unfamiliar language, perseverance when communication is challenging and an appreciation of cultures and perspectives beyond their own. In doing so, we provide strong foundations for further language learning at secondary school and encourage children to approach languages with curiosity, openness and enthusiasm.
Through engaging opportunities to listen, speak, read and write, pupils are enriched by experiences that develop curiosity, confidence and cultural understanding, gaining the skills and enthusiasm to excel as thoughtful, courageous and increasingly independent language learners.

PSHE, RSE & Promoting British Values
Statutory Relationships & Health Education Knowledge Snapshot Progression of Skills & Vocabulary Being me in My World Celebrating Difference Changing Me Dreams & Goals Healthy Me Relationships
PSHE is about understanding ourselves, valuing others and developing the confidence to navigate life with kindness, resilience and responsibility.
.At Beech Grove, we believe that PSHE is fundamental to helping every child grow into a confident, healthy, respectful and responsible individual. Through our PSHE curriculum, we equip children with the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to recognise and manage emotions, build positive relationships, make informed choices and care for their physical and mental wellbeing. Following the Jigsaw PSHE programme from EYFS to Year 6, learning develops progressively as children grow, revisiting and deepening important ideas so that they are increasingly able to understand themselves, relate positively to others and make sense of the world around them.
Through an ambitious and carefully sequenced curriculum, we teach children to reflect, communicate, make thoughtful choices and understand the impact their actions can have on themselves and others. They learn about identity and belonging, similarities and differences, hopes and aspirations, physical and mental health, relationships and the changes they experience as they grow. Alongside developing knowledge, children build the social and emotional skills to recognise and regulate their feelings, listen to different viewpoints, resolve conflict, show empathy, persevere through challenges and know when and how to seek help.
As they progress through school, they explore increasingly complex ideas including rights and responsibilities, democracy, stereotypes, prejudice and discrimination, helping them develop the confidence to stand up for themselves and others and to challenge behaviour that is unfair or unkind.
PSHE extends far beyond a weekly lesson and is reflected in the relationships, values and everyday experiences that shape life at Beech Grove. We create safe and respectful opportunities for children to talk, listen, question and reflect, while working in partnership with families as children develop their understanding of relationships, health and wellbeing. Through the Jigsaw PSHE mindful approach, children also develop emotional awareness, concentration, self-regulation and strategies that support their wellbeing. By celebrating difference, encouraging aspiration and nurturing kindness, courage and respect, we help children develop a strong sense of their own worth alongside an understanding of their responsibilities towards others, preparing them for the opportunities, relationships and challenges of life beyond primary school.
Through engaging opportunities to explore, discuss and reflect, pupils are enriched by experiences that develop self-awareness, empathy and resilience, gaining the confidence to excel as healthy, compassionate and responsible individuals who are prepared to contribute positively to their communities and to life in modern Britain.
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) Consultation
At Beech Grove Primary School, we believe that Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE), including Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE), works best when schools and families work in partnership.
As part of the review of our PSHE and RSHE Policy, parents, carers, staff, governors and pupils were given opportunities to contribute their views. Parents and carers were invited to read the draft policy before completing a consultation questionnaire.
We would like to thank everyone who took the time to share their feedback. Responses were overwhelmingly positive, with parents expressing confidence in the school's age-appropriate approach to teaching relationships, health, wellbeing and safety.

PHONICS AND EARLY READING
Expectations of Progress
At its heart, phonics is about giving every child the tools, confidence and independence to unlock the joy of reading.
At Beech Grove, we believe that learning to read is one of the most important foundations we can give every child. Reading opens the door to learning across the curriculum, develops children's understanding of the world and gives them access to the imagination, knowledge and enjoyment found within books. Through our rigorous and systematic Read Write Inc. Phonics programme, children learn the sounds of the English language and how to blend these sounds to read words accurately. From the beginning of Reception, children build their phonic knowledge progressively, applying what they know to carefully matched books so that they experience success, develop confidence and increasingly see themselves as readers.
Through lively, carefully structured daily teaching, we help children develop accuracy, fluency, comprehension and a love of reading. Children learn to recognise sounds quickly, blend them to read unfamiliar words and use their growing phonic knowledge to support spelling and writing. Books are closely matched to the sounds children know, enabling them to practise decoding successfully before developing greater fluency, expression and understanding. Children regularly talk and work with a partner, ensuring that everyone is actively participating, thinking and practising throughout each lesson. As their knowledge becomes increasingly secure, children move from sounding out words towards reading them automatically and with a storyteller's voice, freeing their attention to focus increasingly on meaning and enjoyment.
We are committed to ensuring that every child receives the teaching and support they need to become a successful reader. Children are regularly assessed so that teaching is closely matched to their stage of learning, with groups adjusted as they progress and additional one-to-one practice provided for children who need extra support. Reading continues beyond the phonics lesson through carefully matched books at home, daily opportunities to enjoy stories and a wider culture in which books and reading are valued and celebrated.
We work in partnership with families so that children can practise familiar sounds and books at home while also experiencing the pleasure of sharing stories together. Our aim is not simply for children to complete a phonics programme, but for every child to leave early reading with the fluency, confidence and enthusiasm that enables them to access the wider curriculum and continue their journey as a lifelong reader. This builds directly upon Beech Grove's existing commitment that reading is a top priority and that no child should be allowed to fall behind.
Through engaging and carefully sequenced opportunities to read, practise and succeed, pupils are enriched by stories and language that build confidence, fluency and a love of books, gaining the skills and independence to excel as enthusiastic and successful readers.
Our aims are to teach children to:
The 5 principles below underpin our teaching:
Praise – Children learn quickly in a positive climate.
Pace – Good pace is essential to the lesson.
Purpose – Every part of the lesson has a specific purpose.
Passion – This is a very prescriptive programme. It is the energy, enthusiasm and passion that teachers put into the lesson that bring the teaching and learning to life!
Participation – A feature of RWI lessons is partner work and the partners ‘teaching’ each other (based on research which states that we learn 70% of what we talk about with our partner and 90% of what we teach).
For those children needing frequent repetition, 'pinny time' is carried out in EYFS classes. For those children at risk of falling behind, formal 1:1 tutoring sessions are implemented by the support staff working across year groups to address the gaps.
Further information for parents
Reading opens the curriculum. At Beech Grove we support the children to become fluent readers. Our expectation is that children read 60-70 words per minute at the blue level and up to 90 words per minute when they progress to grey books. Please watch this example clip of a child in Year 2 reading; we make sure the children at Beech Grove can read with similar fluency and speed.
At home, you can do several things to help your child increase their fluency:
Further guidance for parents and carers to help you support your child at home:
https://www.ruthmiskin.com/parentsandcarers/
/docs/Parent-Carer_Information_Booklet_1__1_.pdf
/docs/Parent-Carer_Information_Booklet_2.pdf
"Children are made readers on the laps of their parents"
Phonics is a way of teaching children to read skillfully.
They are taught how to:
Children can then use this knowledge to ‘decode’ new words that they see or hear. This is the first important step to learning to read.
Research shows that when phonics is taught in a structured way – starting with the easiest sounds and progressing through to the most complex – it is the most effective way of teaching young children to read. It is particularly helpful for children aged 5 to 7.
Almost all children who receive good teaching of phonics will learn the skills they need to tackle new words. They can then go on to read any kind of text fluently and confidently, and read for enjoyment.
Children who have been taught phonics also tend to read more accurately than those taught using other methods, such as ‘look and say’. This includes children who find learning difficult to read, for example those who have dyslexia. At Beech Grove we use the RWI scheme for teaching phonics.
Please see www.gov.uk/government/collections/phonics for more information.
Children learn their sounds in groups, building to using these groups of sounds to read and spell words in Word Time sessions. To begin with there are 6 groups in set 1.
As children progress into learning set 2 sounds they will move from ditty books onto books with one, longer story. RWI lessons will contain time to learn new sounds, existing sound practice, time for reading and also writing.
Children begin to learn that there are multiple ways to read and spell some sounds. They are reminded of one way and learn another, new way.
Please click here to see the Sounds for Sets 1, 2 and 3
'Green' words are phonetically decodable words that the children learn to read. They allow children to become fluent readers because regular reading of these words mean that they become familiar and are able to recognise/read them on sight. They can then use their knowledge of these words to read similar words more quickly. The following are not an exhaustive list of the only words that children will read but instead are an indication of the types of words that will be read at each stage. Children are not tested on these as reading or spelling tests but their ability to read them may be used to inform us of their progress.
The Green words build in stages, called 'Word Time' lessons and during these sessions the children use their recently learnt sounds to segment and blend words.
These are words that children will need to learn on sight because they contain parts that are not decodable. They are arranged into groups according to the colour of the books that they appear in. They might only be red words until a specific sound is learnt or because people pronounce them differently in different parts of the country.
Fred is our RWI mascot/friend. He can only speak in sounds though, so we have to help him learn to say words, instead of sounds. For example Fred says 'c-a-t' instead of cat. We also teach him not to add 'uh' to our sounds in order to keep them pure. For example we say 'c' and not 'cuh'.
We use 'Fred Fingers' to help make the transition between oral sounding out and spelling with magnetic letters or on paper.
Firstly we count how many sounds we can hear:
"cat, c-a-t, 3 sounds".
Then we hold up that many fingers.
For each sound we use our other hand to squeeze a Fred Finger and say the sound
Then we use our free hand to 'sweep' over our Fred Fingers and to blend the sounds into a word
Watch out - words such as fish needs 3 Fred Fingers - "f-i-sh". Words such as flight need 4 Fred Fingers - "f-l-igh-t".
As children become more confident with their sounds and spelling words they will move away from using their Fred Fingers and instead rely on sounding out in their head.
After children have learned enough sounds they will begin to read 'Ditty' books in their RWI lessons, as well as continuing Speedy Sounds and Word Time sessions. Ditty books contain 3 short stories that the children read and these stories are made up from green and red words.
Following Ditty books children continue to read groups of books that have been specially written to support progress through the scheme.
Each colour band contains 10 main books, with extra books to support non-fiction reading as well. Children are taught to read the 'green' and 'red' words at the beginning of each book, before checking understanding using the 'vocab check' page. The children also talk about the upcoming story to make links to their own experiences before reading the book, usually 3 times. The first time is to practise decoding the words, the second time is to practise expression and the third time is to read for comprehension. Each book focuses on a particular sound or set of sounds, allowing the children to practise the sounds that they have been learning most recently. Adults will move their group through the books, picking and choosing books that they feel will best support the learning of their group.
Research has shown that incorporating nonsense words into teaching reading can be an effective way to establish blending and segmenting skills. However it is important to ensure that children understand that they are reading nonsense words (and why) so that they are not confused by trying to read the words for meaning. By reading nonsense words children develop their ability to decode individual sounds and then blend them together to read. They are an indicator of early reading skills and work as a quick, reliable and valid way of assessing children.

INFORMATION FOR PARENTS
Keeping Children Safe in Education 2026
Working Together to Safeguard Children 2026
Beech Grove Safeguarding Statement
We recognise our moral and statutory responsibility to safeguard and promote the welfare of all pupils.
We endeavour to provide a safe and welcoming environment where children are respected and valued.
We are alert to the signs of abuse and neglect and follow our procedures to ensure pupils receive effective support, protection and justice.
Beech Grove Primary School aims to work in close partnership with parents to support the children in every way possible. However, there is a clear responsibility on all schools to ensure they work together with other agencies to safeguard and promote the welfare of all children.
As a result, if concerns are raised within the school, or a child or parent reports a situation involving possible abuse, we are required to refer such matters to the appropriate Children’s Services, in line with Government and Somerset Council policy.
Beech Grove Primary School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Consequently all adults working in school are required to complete a DBS (Disclosure and Barring Service) Enhanced Police Check.
We are fully committed to ensuring that consistent effective safeguarding procedures are in place to support families, children and staff at school. All concerns are passed through the members of staff who are trained as "Designated Child Protection Officers" in school in compliance with the "sharing of information" guidance.
The Designated Safeguarding Lead is Ms Karen Turnbull, Deputy Headteacher. Ms Turnbull is supported by the Deputy Safeguarding Leads: Mrs Mandie Huggett, Miss Claire Joyce and Miss Sarah Eades.
If you have any serious concerns about your child or any other pupil at Beech Grove Primary School please do not hesitate to contact the Designated Safeguarding Lead who knows who to contact for the best advice and help and is experienced in using the appropriate degree of confidentiality.
For the best interests of all our children we use the following safeguarding measures:
Cause for Concern
Teachers are asked to report any causes for concern to the School Safeguarding Team using 'CPOMS' (Child Protection Online Management System).
This electronic system is used by many schools and enables the Safeguarding Team to effectively monitor pupils across the school.
Any concerns will be shared with parents as early as possible as more often that not there are extremely reasonable explanations for the concern. Concerns may range from children being visibly upset to persistent lateness to children ‘disclosing’ concerns.
Attendance
All lateness and absences are recorded by the Attendance Co-ordinator, Mrs Mandie Huggett.
Reasons will be sought for all absence or lateness. Attendance is monitored through these systems and referrals to the Safeguarding Team can be made. Parents will always be informed of concerns around attendance at the earliest point. If attendance concerns continue the school will refer to the Education Welfare Officer.
It may be helpful for parents to know that the Local Authority requires Headteachers to report any obvious or suspected case of child abuse which includes non-accidental injury, severe physical neglect, emotional abuse and/or sexual abuse. This procedure is intended to protect children at risk and schools are encouraged to take the attitude that where there are grounds for suspicion it is better to be safe than sorry. This does mean that Headteachers risk upsetting some parents by reporting a case, which on investigation proves unfounded. In such circumstances, it is hoped that parents, appreciating how difficult it is for Headteachers to carry out this delicate responsibility, would accept that the Headteacher was acting in what were believed to be the child’s best interests.
Useful Links
Below are some useful links of websites that provide further information on a range of safeguarding relating topics:

Maths
Reception Map Year 1 Map Year 2 Map Year 3 Map Year 4 Map Year 5 Map Year 6 Map Calculations GuidanceMaths Progression
Mathematics helps us recognise patterns, solve problems and make sense of the world around us.
At Beech Grove, we believe that every child can succeed in mathematics. More than simply learning to calculate, mathematics empowers children to think logically, reason carefully and approach challenges with confidence. As a subject woven throughout our curriculum, mathematics encourages pupils to discover patterns, explore relationships and create solutions to real-world problems. We equip children with the knowledge, skills and understanding to become fluent mathematicians who can apply their learning confidently in everyday life and future learning.
Through carefully sequenced learning, rich mathematical discussions and practical experiences, children develop a deep understanding of number, calculation, measurement, geometry and statistics. We teach pupils to think like mathematicians by identifying patterns, making connections, explaining their reasoning and justifying their ideas. Through this approach, children learn that mathematics is not simply about finding the correct answer; it is about understanding concepts, persevering through challenges and developing the confidence to think critically and independently.
Our mastery approach enables all children to build secure foundations while exploring mathematical concepts in depth. Through the use of concrete resources, visual representations and mathematical talk, pupils develop strong conceptual understanding alongside fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills. We encourage children to learn from mistakes, value different strategies and recognise that resilience and perseverance are essential components of mathematical success.
Learning is enriched through meaningful opportunities to apply mathematics across the curriculum and beyond the classroom. Whether measuring and analysing data in science, interpreting information in geography, designing and creating in design technology or solving practical everyday problems, children experience mathematics as a relevant and purposeful part of life. Through these experiences, pupils develop confidence, curiosity and independence while recognising the important role mathematics plays in understanding and shaping the world around them.
Through engaging opportunities to explore mathematical ideas, pupils are enriched by experiences that develop curiosity, resilience and logical thinking, gaining the confidence and understanding to excel as capable, independent and enthusiastic mathematicians.

Music
Music Overview AMusic Overview BMusic ProgressionExample Unit OverviewMusic Development Plan
Please scroll down to the bottom of this page to see our recent performances
At its heart, music is about expressing ourselves, connecting with others and experiencing the joy of creating something together.
At Beech Grove, we believe music has the power to bring people together, build confidence and give every child another way to express themselves. Our ambitious music curriculum, supported by Sing Up Music and Charanga, develops children as singers, instrumentalists, composers, performers and thoughtful listeners. From their earliest experiences of exploring sound and keeping a steady beat to increasingly sophisticated composition and ensemble performance, children progressively develop their musical knowledge, skills and vocabulary. They encounter music from different times, places, traditions and cultures, broadening their understanding of both music and the people and communities who create it.
Through practical, creative music-making, we teach children to think and work like musicians. They learn to listen closely and respond thoughtfully, explore the inter-related dimensions of music, sing with increasing accuracy and expression, and play a range of tuned and untuned instruments with growing fluency and control. Children improvise and compose, explore rhythm, melody and harmony, use different forms of musical notation and learn to rehearse, refine and evaluate their work. As they make music independently and with others, they develop creativity, concentration, perseverance and the ability to listen, respond and contribute as part of an ensemble. This progression is reflected strongly in the curriculum, moving from early experimentation with sound to increasingly complex composition, improvisation and musical organisation.
Music reaches far beyond the classroom at Beech Grove. Children have opportunities to learn instruments through specialist tuition, including provision from Somerset Music and Rocksteady, alongside additional instrumental experiences such as ukulele. They experience live music, attend local performances and join with other schools for singing and musical events. Our active school choir performs at school celebrations and within the local community, giving children the experience of using music to bring joy to others and contribute to something bigger than themselves. Performance is an important part of school life, from concerts and celebrations throughout the year to the culmination of children's primary journey through performance in Year 6. These experiences allow children to discover talents and interests, experience the excitement and responsibility of performing for an audience, build confidence and self-belief and, above all, experience the shared joy of making music together..
Through engaging opportunities to listen, create and perform, pupils are enriched by musical experiences that develop creativity, confidence and a sense of belonging, gaining the skills and self-belief to excel as expressive, thoughtful and enthusiastic musicians.

Science
Year A OverviewYear B Overview
Science ProgressionWorking Scientifically Progression
At its heart, science is about being curious about the world, asking questions and using evidence to discover how and why things happen.
At Beech Grove, we believe that science enables children to make sense of the world around them and inspires them to keep asking why. Through an ambitious and carefully sequenced curriculum, children build secure scientific knowledge and vocabulary across biology, chemistry and physics, developing their understanding of living things, materials and the physical processes that shape our world. From observing plants, animals, materials and seasonal change in the early years of their scientific learning to exploring increasingly complex ideas such as forces, electricity, Earth and space, evolution and the human body, we equip children with the knowledge and curiosity to explain what they observe and make connections between different areas of science.
Through practical and purposeful enquiry, we teach children to think and work like scientists. They learn to ask scientific questions, make careful observations, identify patterns, make predictions and plan investigations that help them find answers. Children learn to select and use equipment appropriately, measure accurately, record and present their findings and use results and evidence to draw conclusions. As they progress through school, they become increasingly confident in deciding how to investigate a question, recognising the importance of fair and comparative testing, considering the reliability of evidence and using their scientific knowledge to explain what they have discovered. We encourage children to question ideas, learn from unexpected results and understand that scientific knowledge develops through curiosity, investigation, evidence and explanation.
Learning is enriched by making purposeful use of the local environment and community so that children can experience science beyond the classroom. Wellington's community farm provides valuable opportunities to investigate living things, habitats and the relationships between organisms and their environments, while children in Years 3 and 4 use the local solar farm to connect their learning with science and technology in the world around them.
Across the school, our local area becomes a place for observation and enquiry as children investigate seasonal change and notice how plants, animals, weather and environments alter over time. These first-hand experiences help children recognise that science is not confined to a lesson or laboratory: it is happening all around them. Through observing closely, investigating practically and applying their knowledge to real places and experiences, children develop curiosity, independence and a growing sense of responsibility for the natural world.
Through engaging opportunities to question, investigate and discover, pupils are enriched by experiences that develop curiosity, independence and critical thinking, gaining the knowledge, skills and confidence to excel as thoughtful, enquiring and scientifically literate learners.
